question: In which year Sir William Jones founded "Asiatic Society of Bengal"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1784**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in **1784**.
 
• The society was established in **Kolkata (then Calcutta)**, which was the capital of British India at the time.
 
• The aim of the society was to promote and further the **research and knowledge of the Asian continent** in various fields such as literature, arts, science, and more.
 
• The society played a crucial role in the **study and understanding of Indian culture, languages, and history**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir William Jones**

 
 
• He was a British philologist, orientalist, and jurist who is best known for his proposition of the existence of a relationship among European and Indian languages, which later led to the development of the concept of the Indo-European language family.
 
• He arrived in Calcutta in 1783 to serve as a judge of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William.
 
• His passion for Asian studies led him to establish the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
 
• Jones was proficient in numerous languages including Latin, Greek, French, and Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic Society of Bengal**
 
 
• The society was originally named "Asiatick Society" and later renamed as the "Asiatic Society of Bengal".
 
• The society's main objective was to inquire into the history, antiquities, arts, sciences, and literature of Asia.
 
• It became a premier institution for the study and research of the rich heritage of India and Asia.
 
• The society published numerous journals and books that contributed significantly to the study of Asian cultures and civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata (Calcutta)**
 
 
• Kolkata, formerly known as Calcutta, was the capital of British India from 1772 to 1911.
 
• It is located on the east bank of the Hooghly River in the Indian state of West Bengal.
 
• The city played a key role in the cultural and intellectual renaissance of India during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• Kolkata remains an important cultural, commercial, and educational hub in India today.
